English Grammar and Composition 51

subject of the sentences.

Grammar point

subject: English_grammar
chapter_title: The -ing form of Verb: Gerund and Participle
text:
When -ing verbs are used to begin or complete sentences (i.e. used as subjects
or objects), they have nominal function (function of a noun) and they are called
gerund. A gerund is also called a verbal- noun. It looks like a verb but functions
like a noun.

subject: English_grammar
chapter_title: The -ing form of Verb: Gerund and Participle
text:
We also use -ing form as the subject of a sentence when the subject is an action
or situation, not a person or thing. In that case, we need a complement or
object at the end.
Examples

subject: English_grammar
chapter_title: The -ing form of Verb: Gerund and Participle
text:
Walking is a good exercise. (-ing verb as subject followed by a
ing-verb linking verb complement linking verb and complement)
Working too hard ruins his health. (-ing verb as subject followed by
ing-verb verb object verb and object)

subject: English_grammar
chapter_title: The -ing form of Verb: Gerund and Participle
text:
When -ing verbs are used after another verb, they are objects.
i) We use -ing verb after various ver s connected with liking or not liking
something: like, love, enjoy, hate
ii) We use -ing verb after mind in negative statements to say that we are
not angry or unhappy about something:
| would like to buy a new car. | don’t have sufficient money.
| don’t mind lending you some money.
Thanks. Not now.
iii) We use ‘would you mind followed by —ing verb to ask someone to do
something politely.
Would you mind closing the door, please? It’s very cold, isn’t it?
Not at all. | was also thinking the same.

Grammar Focus
As indicated above, a participle can be made by adding ing to a verb. However,
it becomes a participle only when adding ing to the verb makes it function as an

functions like an adjective; it modifies a noun or pronoun.

56 English Grammar and Composition
Grammar Point
Gerund vs Participle
Gerund
People are confused about the use of gerund and present participle because
of their similarities in form. Both are formed by adding ‘ing’to a verb. There is

subject: English_grammar
chapter_title: The -ing form of Verb: Gerund and Participle
text:
another similarity and that is the fact that both gerund and present participle
indicate some action or state of being. However, there are differences between
them which is highlighted here.
Participle

subject: English_grammar
chapter_title: The -ing form of Verb: Gerund and Participle
text:
As seen above, present participles are formed by adding ing to a verb. However,
it becomes a participle only when adding ing to the verb makes it function as an
adjective. It is also called a verbal noun.
What is the difference between Gerund and Participle?
A gerund is a verbal noun (verb made noun by adding ing) that looks like a
verb but functions as a noun. It is called a verbal noun.

subject: English_grammar
chapter_title: The -ing form of Verb: Gerund and Participle
text:
e A (present) participle is also formed by adding ‘ing’ to base form of an
action verb but it functions like an adjective. It isa a verbal adjective.
They are structurally the same but functionally different. A gerund functions
as anoun but a participle functions as an adjective.
